explanation: Robes in shades of saffron and ochre were once dyed with plants such as jackfruit wood. Korean monks wear grey, many Japanese monks black, and Thai nuns white.

claims.text: Buddhist monks in Thailand traditionally wear robes in shades of orange, from saffron to ochre.
Thai Buddhist monks do not traditionally wear white, black or grey robes.
Theravada monks' robes were traditionally dyed with plant materials, including jackfruit heartwood.
Korean Buddhist monks usually wear grey robes.
Many Japanese Buddhist priests wear black robes.
Buddhist nuns in Thailand (mae chi) wear white.

Thai monks do not traditionally wear white, black or grey robes; white is worn by lay devotees and by mae chi.
Thai forest monks traditionally dye their robes with boiled jackfruit heartwood.
Korean Buddhist monks usually wear grey robes.

claimResults.note: Rival test: forest-tradition monks wear darker brown-ochre, still in the orange family. White, grey and black are not Thai monastic colours.
